newsitem.title: JAPAN: Thailand did not request financial support--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Thailand did not request financial support--BOJ.

text.p: Thailand's Central Bank Governor Rerngchai Marakanond did not ask Japan for any financial support during a meeting on Thursday with Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita, BOJ executive director Takashi Anzai told reporters on Thursday.
"There was no request from Thailand for financial support," Anzai said.
The Thai central bank governor explained to the BOJ governor the country's moves towards a managed floating rate system and its financial situation, he added.
Anzai also quoted the Thai governor as saying that the markets were gradually settling down and that the Thai authorities would take appropriate measures as necessary.
Anzai said there were explanations about measures the Thai authorities were considering, but he declined to indicate what they were.
Anzai quoted Matsushita as telling Rerngchai that it was important for the Thai economy and Asia as a whole that the foreign exchange markets settle down.
Anzai also quoted Matsushita as saying that he would like to keep a careful watch over the Thai situation.
The two central bank governors agreed that cooperation was important, Anzai said.
"After listening to what the Thais had to say, my impression was that the situation is not as serious as the media and the markets think," Anzai said.
Asked whether the two central bank governors talked about joint intervention to support the baht, Anzai said there was no such discussion.
The Thai side explained that it was receiving technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), he added.
